title: Trade desk: free-form amounts
description: The trade desk used to propose only the closed menu the engine lists (give 0 to 3 trade goods for 0 to 3, commodity swaps up to 3, one asset plus a price). Now the proposer can stage any amounts either purse covers, equal or not, and the engine accepts the deal as a free-form id. Both purses are public, so the steppers stop there.

shots.heading: Unequal amounts, desktop
shots.caption: Give 3 trade goods, receive 5 trade goods and 1 commodity: no listed deal, yet Propose is enabled. The status says the deal is custom and not rated; the steppers read 'any amount up to N' for each purse.

shots.heading: Commodities, 4 for 2
shots.caption: An unequal commodity trade (4 of ours for the partner's 2). Commodities become trade goods on arrival as usual.

shots.heading: Phone 390x844
shots.caption: The same desk on a phone.

shots.heading: Before: a server without the flag
shots.caption: A decision without details.free_form keeps the closed list: a combination off the list (2 trade goods for 1 commodity) is refused with the reason and nearest listed deals.

notes.title: How it is sent
notes.text: A free-form deal is submitted as an option id such as x;gt=3;rt=5;rc=1; (g = what the proposer gives, r = what they receive; t trade goods, c commodities, n note, a action card, s secret, f fragments). The server accepts ids with the prefix the decision announces (details.free_form); the engine parses and checks legality exactly as for listed deals (neighbours, holdings, Hubris, action-card rule). Listed shapes still go as their own id and keep their net rating.
